newsitem.title: USA: Conn Gov gets applications for Treasurer - paper.
newsitem.headline: Conn Gov gets applications for Treasurer - paper.

text.p: Connecticut's Governor John Rowland told the Hartford Courant he had gotten eight to nine applications for Treasurer, the paper said Friday.

The present Treasurer, Christopher Burnham, said in late June he would resign to take a job with a Stamford investment firm that held a state contract during his tenure, but he did not disclose the date he would leave.

The applications, which all were from Republicans, included Senator Win Smith of Milford, former Treasurer Joan Kemler, Paul Silvester of the treasurer's office, and Darien resident Steven Hart, who works with Burnham as chairman of the state's Investment Advisory Council.
Senator William Nickerson of Greenwich has taken himself out of contention.
